scopeDecisions.decision: Managed-infrastructure surfaces stay out of scope: backups, backupSchedules, restore, clone and point-in-time recovery (enabling it, its seven-day version retention and the read_time window it widens). No emulator user drives them; they are operated with gcloud or Terraform against production. Only the values databases.get reports for them (pointInTimeRecoveryEnablement, versionRetentionPeriod, earliestVersionTime) are compared. fireemu refuses these methods, and a databases.patch that enables point-in-time recovery, with a documented refusal instead of pretending to serve them.
scopeDecisions.supersedes: 2026-09-18 FS-CONFIG-LIFECYCLE exclusion, except for the parts C2 brings back

scopeDecisions.decision: Named Native database create, delete and patch, and managed exportDocuments and importDocuments over gs:// URIs, are in scope as REST long-running operations with production's request validation, operation shapes and post-state. fireemu writes and reads managed exports in the emulated Cloud Storage bucket, and a production export must import into fireemu and a fireemu export into production.

Values only production can give meaning to follow what production answers: the locations catalog (locations.list and locations.get), freeTier (true only for the project's free-tier database), locationId as created, and the refusal of an unknown location, a customer-managed encryption key and resource tags.

bulkDeleteDocuments, changeStreams and userCreds follow what a Standard edition production database answers: production serves bulkDeleteDocuments, so fireemu implements it; production refuses changeStreams and userCreds on Standard ('This operation requires an Enterprise database.'), so fireemu refuses them the same way.
The comparison runs against the strict profile. The emulator profile keeps the official emulator's behavior (any database materializes on first touch) and is not closure evidence.

scopeDecisions.decision: Production runs touch only named databases the run creates in fireemu-oracle-query (prefix cfg), plus a per-run Cloud Storage bucket; (default) belongs to FS-QUERY-INDEX and is only read. A request that production rejects before it reaches any resource (a foreign project, an invalid id) may name other resources.

scopeDecisions.decision: The Admin API is observed over REST v1 in full; representative cases are also observed over gRPC google.firestore.admin.v1 (database create, get, list and delete; index create and get; export and import; operation get), because the Node FirestoreAdminClient, which the documented scheduled-export sample uses, speaks gRPC by default.

Time-to-live is observed as configuration (the ttlConfig state transitions, removal, the list filter) and as the behavior before deletion (an expired document stays readable). Production deletes expired documents 'typically within 24 hours' with no guarantee, so the deletion instant is not a contract; fireemu keeps deleting on its virtual-clock sweep.

Creating and deleting (default), and a project with no (default), cannot be observed in fireemu-oracle-query, whose (default) belongs to FS-QUERY-INDEX, and no new project can be created. They are observed in fireemu-fs-bisect-0924a when it is cleaned up, after the FS-DATA-WRITE bisection there has finished and before the project is deleted.

Production long-running operations progress on their own schedule (an index takes minutes to build, an index operation stays PROCESSING after the index is READY, a deleted index keeps serving queries for a while, an exemption takes minutes to apply). Recordings compare the first response, every state the recording polls through after normalizing how many polls saw it, and the settled end state. fireemu must answer the same shapes and pass through the same states; how long it stays in each is not compared.

scopeDecisions.decision: A project the credential cannot use is answered with production's 403 PERMISSION_DENIED (ErrorInfo CONSUMER_INVALID) only when the configuration opts in: under the strict profile, projects.unknownProjects = "refuse" makes the daemon's project the only one that exists. The default keeps serving every project in its own session, because parallel test workers commonly use one project id each, and emulators.singleProjectMode is not reused because firebase init writes it as true. The project-boundary comparison runs against the opt-in configuration (conformance/fs-config-lifecycle.fireemu.json).

fireemu-fs-bisect-0924a is a closure-evidence project for two purposes only: FS-CONFIG-LIFECYCLE's creation and deletion of (default) and a project without it (C9), and FS-DATA-WRITE's boundary exploration. Its configuration and use history are kept with the sandbox records, and a recording there first checks the sandbox ledger that no other lane is using it.

The managed-export partition checksum (export_metadata field 2.5) is a known divergence: production's value is a digest nobody can reproduce and production imports an export whose checksum is 0 without verifying it, so fireemu writes 0 and does not verify checksums on import.

The Admin API is served under both profiles. Its effects only follow a call the official emulator does not serve, so no existing request is newly refused; it is listed as fireemuOnly in spec/compatibility/contract.json and in the CHANGELOG with its configuration keys.

evidence.comparisonRules: MATCH_NONDETERMINISTIC rows agree with one of production's two recordings of the same starting state; each is listed in productionVariations with why production varied and which recording it matches. MATCH_RELABELED rows are listings equal under a one-to-one renaming of opaque id and instant symbols, whose numbering follows the order the server listed entries.

productionVariations.reason: A GET of a database deleted moments earlier answers 'Requested database was not found.' while the deletion settles and 'Project ... or database ... does not exist.' once it has; which one a recording sees depends on timing.
How many of an export operation's transitional states a poll sees depends on timing (one recording saw PROCESSING before SUCCESSFUL); the states and their order agree (C10).
Right after (default) is deleted production still lists its indexes for a while, then answers NOT_FOUND; one recording listed them, the other was already refused.
